title: Ham & Cabbage Noodle Bowls
description: Tender cabbage, noodles, and diced ham make a fast skillet meal that is especially handy for using leftovers.
substitutions: Use cooked sausage instead of ham.
Use any short pasta if egg noodles are unavailable.

steps.text: Soften the cabbage and warm the ham.

cookSteps.text: Cook 8 ounces egg noodles according to the package. Drain, reserving a splash of cooking water.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet. Add 3 cups sliced cabbage and cook 6–8 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally.
Add 1 1/2 cups diced cooked ham, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Cook 2 minutes to heat through.
Add the drained noodles and toss. Add a splash of reserved cooking water if the noodles seem dry.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet or microwave with a spoonful of water.

title: White Bean Tomato Toast Pizzas
description: Crisp bread topped with mashed white beans, tomato, and cheese for a quick pantry lunch.
equipment: sheet pan or toaster oven tray
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use salsa instead of diced tomatoes for a different flavor.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven or toaster oven to 425°F. Mash 1 cup white beans with a fork until chunky.
Spread the beans over 4 bread slices. Top with 1/2 cup drained diced tomatoes, 3/4 cup shredded cheese, and 1/2 teaspoon Italian seasoning.
Bake 8–10 minutes until the bread edges are crisp and the cheese is melted.

storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate the bean topping up to 3 days and assemble new toast when ready.

title: One-Pot Peas & Parmesan Rice
description: A soft, savory rice dish with peas and Parmesan made from inexpensive staples in one pot.
substitutions: Use frozen mixed vegetables instead of peas.
Use shredded cheddar instead of Parmesan for a different creamy rice.

cookSteps.text: Combine 1 cup rice and 2 cups broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce to low.
Cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Scatter 1 cup frozen peas over the rice, cover again, and cook 5 minutes more.
Remove from the heat. Stir in 1 tablespoon butter, 1/2 cup Parmesan, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Let stand covered 5 minutes before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat with a splash of water or broth.

title: Banana Cinnamon French Toast Bites
description: Small cinnamon French-toast pieces with banana, designed to rescue bread that is getting dry.
substitutions: Use diced apple instead of banana and cook it a few minutes longer.

steps.text: Cut the bread and mix the custard.
Coat and cook the bread bites.

cookSteps.text: Cut 4 bread slices into bite-size squares. Whisk 2 eggs, 1/4 cup milk, and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon in a bowl.
Toss the bread pieces briefly in the egg mixture until coated but not falling apart.
Melt 1 teaspoon butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the bread bites 5–7 minutes, turning often, until golden and cooked through.
Add 1 sliced banana for the final 1–2 minutes, turning gently until warmed. Serve right away.

storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat in a skillet or toaster oven.
